response.content: {"visual":{"fullPrompt":"Handheld tight medium close-up, modern social-first beauty campaign photography with editorial tactile energy, 16:9. SCARLETT VEGA stands balanced in the aisle of a moving subway car wearing a fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed to the elbows, dark slim jeans, scuffed black ankle boots and a slouchy dark denim-canvas jacket, a heavy natural-canvas tote slung over one shoulder, small gold hoop earrings and a thin silver ring on her right index finger catching the overhead light. She is caught mid-motion, weight braced through her knees against the lurch of the floor, one hand hooked loosely around a brushed stainless grab pole, the other hand raised and holding the lipstick from (CORAL_LIPSTICK) uncapped in a one-handed grip, the cap pinched between two fingers of the same hand, wrist angled toward her mouth, her chin lifted a fraction and lips just parting — potential energy of the press about to land, no mirror, done entirely by feel. Around her the car interior is fully packed and cramped: molded plastic bench seating in transit orange and blue, riveted brushed-stainless panels and vertical poles, overhead grab bars swinging, scratched windows behind her showing pure black tunnel rush with occasional streaking service lights, blank ad panels above the window line, corrugated grey floor. Anonymous commuters crowd the frame edges in shallow soft focus, shoulders and coat sleeves blurred by handheld micro-shake. Lighting is flat hard overhead fluorescent tubing, slightly green-cyan, hard and unforgiving across skin, with a small punchy specular glare skidding across the glossy surface of the tube and a cool rim of light along the steel pole; whites crisp, shadows lifted and airy, one warm coral accent popping against the cool neutral steel.
